fields.study_design: theoretical essay with ethnographic case illustrations (three weeks of fieldwork in Belo Horizonte in August-September 2013); no formal sampling, data-collection protocol or analysis method
fields.sample_size: three organised land occupations on the outskirts of Belo Horizonte (Eliana Silva, Rosa Leao and Dandara; 300-1,300 families each) and the favela of Nossa Senhora de Fatima in the Aglomerado da Serra (about 50,000 people; some 40 years for trunk infrastructure to become part of the invisible background); number of residents or interviews not stated
fields.effect_measure: qualitative ethnographic illustration of infrastructure as a social and political intermediary; no quantitative estimate
fields.effect_estimate: In the occupations, built on disused private or public land by movements such as the Brigadas Populares and the MLB with university architects and lawyers, residents co-construct water, electricity, shelter and sanitation themselves, which makes infrastructure visible and a basis for community, solidarity and political claims to the right to the city, while knowing they can be evicted at any time; in the old favela, long-established trunk infrastructure has receded into an invisible background that allows residents to lead fuller lives and exercise citizenship. The author argues that infrastructure is a gathering force and political intermediary shaping the rights of the poor to the city and their capacity to claim them; no access, connection or service-level outcome is measured and the legal setting (occupation law, evictions, a judiciary resistant to facilitative laws) is context.
fields.section: Full text (about 20 pages, Theory, Culture and Society manuscript): Introduction; Infrastructure visible (occupations); Infrastructure invisible (favela); Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Introduction (fieldwork statement); section on the occupations; section on the favela; Theory, Culture & Society 31(7-8)

evidence_level: Single-source evidence: a theoretical essay on the social life of infrastructure illustrated by three weeks of fieldwork in land occupations and a favela in Belo Horizonte; no stated method and no access outcome; read in full text 2026-10-04.

notes: ELIGIBILITY FLAG: a theoretical essay with ethnographic illustration; inclusion criteria 3 (empirical evidence) and 4 (access outcome) are doubtful. Strong legal and tenure context (illegal occupations, evictions). Candidate for the criterion-3 audit (A22).
